newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast products mixed following APIs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast products mixed following APIs.

text.p: U.S. West Coast products were mixed late Tuesday following a report which showed neutral changes in crude inventories and drawdowns in gasoline, traders said.
West Coast products, which track both crude and product futures, saw little direction in light activity.
January NYMEX crude set the tone for western products, with futures little changed in ACCESS trade, which follows the release of stock data from the American Petroleum Institute (API).
NYMEX crude eased two cents a barrel during overnight trade after API reported stocks down a seasonal 2.6 million barrels last week.
Gasoline futures firmed after-hours after API showed stocks falling 3.1 million barrels last week. January gasoline on ACCESS climbed around 0.13 cents a gallon to 69.90 cents.
"Gas is bid a little bit better," said a trader when asked how regional products responded to APIs.
CARB-grade gasoline in Los Angeles was bid two cents higher than earlier at 71.50 cents a gallon. Offers rose 1.50 cents to 72.50 cents.
Ongoing outages at Mobil, Chervon, and Unocal refiners also kept traders concerned about supplies.
West Coast distillates, meanwhile, eased despite firmer ACCESS heating oil prices.
Heating oil rose about 0.20 cents after-hours as traders focused on a northeast U.S. drawdown of 748,000 barrels last week.
But Western traders kept their focus on the relative high cost of crude, bidding low sulphur diesel half a cent lower in L.A. to 69.50 cents.
